Initialization, ownership, and concurrency control for shared session buffers and connection state.
Architecture specific handlers for exception resume, register access, breakpoint control, and query extensions.
Full command set, permission assignments, and output filter semantics for the debugger shell.
Sleeping thread register synthesis and scheduler state requirements.
Cache flush safety condition and instruction coherence guarantees.

findings.text: GDB remote session processor that consumes exception context for one stopped CPU and conducts a request response dialogue until architecture handling indicates resume or session teardown. Callers supply populated exception state. The processor announces the stop when already connected and otherwise enters its packet loop. Cited behavior covers only generic dispatch. Architecture specific resume and query extensions live elsewhere.

Dialogue is packet oriented with one reply per inbound packet except for terminal resume or detach conditions that exit without further reply. Session control operations clear breakpoints and connection state. Register and memory operations report or update target state. Breakpoint operations delegate to generic break handling. Thread and query operations report task identity. Unrecognized or resume related inputs fall through to architecture exception handling whose success ends the session. Detach via kill and explicit detach are treated as resume like termination.

Inbound framing waits for a dollar sign, then accumulates payload up to a bounded maximum until a hash sign, then validates a two digit hexadecimal checksum. Positive acknowledgment with a plus sign or negative acknowledgment with a minus sign is emitted through registered IO operations with optional flush, and reception repeats until checksum agreement. Successful reception marks the session connected and yields a null terminated payload.

Error replies use uppercase E followed by two decimal digits derived from the magnitude of the supplied negative error code, terminated with null. The encoding is fixed width and independent of architecture.

Thread references are transmitted as big endian binary identifiers with leading zero bytes suppressed on the wire, guaranteeing at least one encoded byte even for zero values. Integer thread values are first rendered into fixed size big endian form before suppression.

Zero process identifiers, which denote idle or unspecified contexts, are remapped to negative per CPU shadow values derived from the current CPU number, while non zero identifiers pass through unchanged. This preserves distinct thread identities for per CPU stop states.

Thread identifier resolution maps zero and minus one to the currently active CPU shadow, maps a small negative range to per CPU stopped tasks with fallback to idle tasks, rejects other non positive values with diagnostic output and null return, and resolves positive values through the initial PID namespace without taking the task list lock.

After clearing completes, every memory breakpoint slot is in undefined state regardless of prior activity or architecture removal failures, and hardware breakpoint clearing has been requested when the architecture provides it. The operation always reports success. Status handling guarantees this cleared state before reporting the stop signal, so a reconnecting host never inherits stale breakpoints.

Register snapshots prefer architecture register state captured for the selected thread when that thread corresponds to a stopped CPU, and otherwise synthesize an approximate snapshot from scheduler saved state sufficient for stack unwinding. Conversion between architecture register blocks and the generic register array proceeds register by register using per register size descriptors and accessor helpers.

Whole register read always refreshes the generic array from the selected thread and returns its hexadecimal encoding. Whole register and single register updates are refused with invalid argument indication when a foreign thread is selected. Otherwise updates apply to the stopped CPU register block and acknowledge success. Single register access validates the register number against the architecture maximum before any copy.

Memory to hexadecimal conversion copies through an intermediate area using fault safe kernel reads and yields null on fault, otherwise produces null terminated hexadecimal text. Hexadecimal to memory conversion decodes digit pairs through an intermediate area and performs fault safe kernel writes, returning the copy outcome. Hexadecimal integer parsing accepts an optional negation marker and consumes the longest valid digit run, reporting digit count.

Memory read and write requests carry hexadecimal address and length with a separator, with writes adding a data delimiter. Valid encodings attempt fault safe transfer and acknowledge success, while malformed encodings or transfer faults yield invalid argument indication. Binary writes additionally unescape a designated escape byte with decimal value one hundred twenty five using mask value thirty two before copying. Successful writes request instruction cache coherence when the platform marks that operation safe.

Current thread queries report the stopped context through the shadow mapping. Thread list queries enumerate one shadow entry per online CPU followed by process threads with pagination retained across continuations and bounded batch size. Extra info queries report task names for real threads and synthesized CPU labels for shadows, rejecting unknown identifiers. Remote command and architecture feature queries apply only when their build options are enabled.

Explicit detach clears all breakpoints and, on success, acknowledges and marks the session disconnected before emitting its reply, while the kill variant clears breakpoints and disconnects without its own acknowledgment. Reboot is honored only for uppercase R followed by zero, in which case it acknowledges, emits the reply, invokes emergency restart, and marks disconnection. Other arguments leave the session unchanged.

Input output readiness is negative only when no IO operations are registered. In all other cases it is affirmative, including when already connected or when a breakpoint is being set. An optional wait indication is emitted only when requested and not connected, with wording dependent on build configuration and mode.

Debug entry suppresses false stall reports by refreshing soft lockup, clocksource, and RCU stall detectors together. The soft lockup component records a synchronous touch and a deferred report timestamp using CPU local storage.

Provides externally callable GDB session handling, breakpoint clearing, register translation in both directions, and fault tolerant hexadecimal memory codecs for use by architecture and core debug paths.

Provides externally callable soft lockup touch synchronization and common state establishment, teardown, and command dispatch, plus a header fallback that reports pass through for exception events when full handling is absent.

KDB command entry that accepts a null terminated command line and returns a disposition code indicating success, permission denial, unknown command, or debugger control flow. Empty input and interrupt cleared state yield success without action.

Command processing supports tokenization with quoting, escaping, comment termination, and output filter separation, with bounded argument count and line length. Lookup prefers exact and abbreviated matches before prefix fallback, enforces permission gating, and otherwise attempts address interpretation with symbol display. Repeat behavior and error suppression are governed by command flags and an explicit dash prefix.

Permission evaluation always grants universally safe operations, restricts caller supplied permissions to the defined enable mask, and augments permissions for argument less invocations before intersecting with command requirements. Evaluation yields a boolean grant decision.

Context establishment captures the active CPU number and the corresponding stopped task and register block for later command use and always reports success. Teardown resets those cached values to an empty state and likewise reports success.
When full dispatch is unavailable, exception events are unconditionally reported as pass through without inspecting event details.

Observed state includes per CPU stop records holding a task pointer and architecture register block, a session object carrying CPU index, signal, exception vector and code, register block pointer, selected thread identifiers, query pagination, and pass through control, plus per register size descriptors and a command table with name, abbreviation length, flags, and handler. Exact widths and ordering beyond these uses are not shown.

Task resolution for positive identifiers relies on RCU protection without explicit task list locking, and thread enumeration occurs while other CPUs are held in the debugger, implying a stopped world assumption. Soft lockup refresh uses CPU local writes without cross CPU synchronization, and packet exchange assumes exclusive ownership of shared command buffers by the debugging CPU.

Fault safe memory copies can fail and must be treated as invalid argument rather than partial success. Register and memory updates targeting a non current thread are refused to avoid cross thread corruption. Single register numbers outside the architecture maximum and malformed address encodings are rejected without side effects.

Session teardown unconditionally discards breakpoints, so detach and reconnect lose prior breakpoint state. Reboot handling invokes a non returning emergency path and must not be followed by normal reply processing. Debug entry must refresh stall detectors to avoid spurious lockup reports during prolonged stops.

Command parsing enforces fixed limits on line length and argument count, rejecting oversized input with diagnostic output rather than truncation. Binary memory decoding expands escape sequences in place and requires adequate input buffering. Thread list pagination state persists across queries and must be reset by starting a new full listing.

Wire framing uses dollar sign for opening, hash sign for closing, plus sign for acknowledgment, and minus sign for negative acknowledgment, with two digit hexadecimal checksums and bounded payload size. Replies use fixed single letter prefixes for stop notification, status, error, thread list continuation, and acknowledgment, with thread identifiers as suppressed leading zero hexadecimal big endian values.

Debugger limits include a fixed memory breakpoint table size with active and undefined states, a fixed register count and byte size with per register sizes, a bounded thread query batch size, fixed command line and argument limits, and permission bit groups including always safe and no argument augmented sets. Pass through and not found dispositions are distinct control outcomes.
